text:
IncidentBot: paging: high error rate detected on inference cluster us-west-2-gpu-3, error class=cache-miss-coherency, p95 latency spiking; currently 12% 5m error rate, alert threshold 2%
Sam (oncall): acked, jumping in. grabbing logs and traces.
Priya (sre): seen a surge from a single customer prefix group, looks like KV prefix cache entries are returning stale keys causing correctness failures -> 500s from model runtime process.
Jordan (runtime): confirmed. root cause looks like concurrent writes to prefix namespace + LRU eviction race under heavy prefix churn. We are seeing KV cache version mismatch between nodes.
Lena (eng-runtime): proposed immediate mitigation: 1) disable prefix-based caching for the impacted model family (redwood/gptx-3b-v2) 2) set short-term per-prefix read-through bypass for critical customers 3) apply rate-shaping to bursty tenants.
Marta (support): can we get a list of impacted customers so we can notify? I already see 3 enterprise tenants with elevated 500s in Support dashboard.
James (ml-runtime): disabling prefix cache will increase token cost and latency but should stop correctness 500s. we should only do it for the model family and a short window.
Sam (oncall): agreed. plan: (A) apply config toggle to turn off prefix/KV cache for redwood/gptx-3b-v2 across us-west-2 cluster (B) inject traffic shaping rule to limit requests >50 rps per tenant for 15m (C) temporarily increase quota for the control-plane health-check bucket so monitoring stays stable. execute in that order.
Priya (sre): I'll create the mitigation runbook steps here.
Priya (sre): Step 1: run command in ops-control (only in us-west-2):
```
# disable prefix cache for model family
opsctl config set runtime.kv_cache.prefix.enabled=false --model redwood/gptx-3b-v2 --region us-west-2 --apply
```
Priya (sre): Step 2: apply tenant-level rate shaping using traffic-police: limit = 50, window=1s, duration=900s
```
traffic-police apply --region us-west-2 --selector "tenant.meta in (ent-123,ent-456,ent-789)" --limit 50/s --duration 15m --reason "kv-coherency-mitigation"
```
Priya (sre): Step 3: bump control-plane monitoring quota so LF health checks don't get rate limited
```
opsctl quota inc --service=monitoring --consumer=control-plane --amount=1000 --region=us-west-2
```
Jordan (runtime): I've run step 1 in dry-run, returning success. Applying now.
Jordan (runtime): Applied prefix cache disable: op-id=op_1732101248, diff: prefix cache -> false across 6 nodes, waiting for propagation.
Sam (oncall): rolling restart not required, runtime checks show nodes switching to bypass path.
Lena (eng-runtime): starting to see 500 rate drop in metrics, p95 latency up ~60ms, but correctness errors drop.
ProdAnalytics: metric snippet: pre-mitigation 5m err=12.4%, post-disable 5m err=2.1% (still above threshold but trending down).
Marta (support): notifying affected customers: ent-123, ent-456, ent-789. Draft message: "We're seeing transient 500s due to cache coherence under load. We've temporarily disabled prefix caching for the model family to ensure correctness; latency may be slightly higher. We're monitoring and will follow up." send?
Sam (oncall): send now. include mitigation steps and ETA 60m to stabilize.
Marta (support): sent to ent-123 and ent-456, ent-789 on Slack. ent-456 requested ETA, asked if we can prioritize their traffic.
Priya (sre): for ent-456 we can add a short-lived elevated rate cap:
```
traffic-police apply --tenant ent-456 --limit 100/s --duration 15m --reason "support-priority"
```
James (ml-runtime): doing that now.
James (ml-runtime): elevated ent-456 to 100/s. monitor for 2 min.
Jordan (runtime): logs show reduced 500s for ent-456 immediately. good sign.
Sam (oncall): next: apply tenant bypass for legacy model versions that still rely on older KV format. This prevents clients sending older prefix signatures from hitting the cache.
Lena (eng-runtime): command to add bypass rule:
```
opsctl config set runtime.kv_cache.bypass_rules += "model:redwood/gptx-3b-v2,version:<2024-08-01,action:bypass" --region us-west-2 --apply
```
Lena (eng-runtime): rule applied op-id=op_1732101355.
Priya (sre): monitoring: overall errors down to 0.9% 5m, p95 latency 220ms (was 160ms baseline).
ProdAnalytics: note: request throughput dropped 18% due to rate shaping; cost expected to increase by ~7% when cache re-enabled.
Marta (support): ent-789 replied: "Thanks, do you have any ETA when cache will be back?"
Sam (oncall): tentative timeline: keep cache disabled for 60 minutes, during that window we'll roll a patched KV eviction fix to a canary node. If canary stable for 30m, roll to rest. total ETA ~90-120m.
Priya (sre): starting on-call handoff note for next rotation:
"Handoff: prefix/KV cache coherence incident. Mitigation applied: prefix cache disabled for redwood/gptx-3b-v2 in us-west-2; tenant rate-shaping in place for ent-123, ent-456(extra), ent-789. Bypass rule deployed for legacy model versions. Watch p95 latency and 5m error rate. Steps to rollback: re-enable prefix cache via opsctl config set runtime.kv_cache.prefix.enabled=true --model redwood/gptx-3b-v2 --region us-west-2 after validating canary."
Sam (oncall): @Priya add the op-ids and Slack links to the handoff ticket.
Priya (sre): added op-ids: op_1732101248, op_1732101355; created incident ticket #INC-2026-0427 and linked runbook.
Marta (support): closing communication loop: ent-456 confirmed degraded but acceptable; ent-123 asked for postmortem.
Jordan (runtime): we'll prepare a short postmortem with timeline and root cause. immediate fix is to harden the eviction logic and add a cache version handshake before serving cached entries.
Lena (eng-runtime): dev plan: add per-prefix version tags and atomically update on write path; add metrics for cache-version-mismatch. target patch ETA 48h, hotfix to canary in 2h.
Sam (oncall): marking incident mitigation as "in progress -> stabilized". Will continue to monitor for 1 hour then consider rollback.
ProdAnalytics: final note: please snapshot logs for the 20m window around 1732101200-1732102000 and export to s3://redwood-incident-archives/1732101234 for postmortem.
James (ml-runtime): snapshot started. export op=exp_1732101500.
Priya (sre): any objections to reverting rate shaping after 30m of stable error rate <1%?
Sam (oncall): no objections. schedule revert in 30m unless new alerts.
Marta (support): logging customer follow-ups and postmortem requests.
IncidentBot: reminder set: follow-up check in 30m.
Sam (oncall): thanks team. handoff notes updated. I'll follow up if anything changes. :thumbsup:
